\section[arrepender]{arrepender — to regret (arrepender-se de)}

\label{lesson:PT-C480-arrepender}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to forgive, then the Portuguese for forgiveness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: arrepender}
\textbf{arrepender} — \textquotedblleft{}to regret (arrepender-se de)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Arrependi-me de não ter estudado mais.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I regretted not having studied more.}
\end{quote}

Reflexive in practice: \emph{arrepender-se de} + noun or infinitive.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{arrepender} is inherited, through Old Portuguese \emph{arrepentir} (EtymDB), from Vulgar Latin \emph{repoenitēre}, built on Latin \emph{paenitēre} \textquotedblleft{}to cause regret\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{arrepender}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{arrepender}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{arrepender}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to forgive, then the Portuguese for forgiveness, then say \emph{arrepender} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does arrepender mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To regret (arrepender-se de)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[o arrependimento]{o arrependimento — regret}

\label{lesson:PT-C480-arrependimento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for forgiveness, then the Portuguese for to regret.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o arrependimento}
\textbf{o arrependimento} — \textquotedblleft{}regret\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Sente arrependimento pelo que disse.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He feels regret for what he said.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{arrepender} with \emph{-imento}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{arrependimento} is built on \emph{arrepender} \textquotedblleft{}to regret\textquotedblright{}, which goes back to Latin \emph{paenitēre} \textquotedblleft{}to cause regret\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).

\section[o remorso]{o remorso — remorse}

\label{lesson:PT-C480-remorso}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to regret, then the Portuguese for regret.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o remorso}
\textbf{o remorso} — \textquotedblleft{}remorse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Depois da mentira, ficou com remorsos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{After the lie, he felt remorse.}
\end{quote}

Often plural: \emph{ter remorsos}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{remorso} is a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{remorsus} \textquotedblleft{}a biting back\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{remordēre} \textquotedblleft{}to bite again\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short): a conscience that bites.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o remorso}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o remorso}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to regret, then the Portuguese for regret, then say \emph{o remorso} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does o remorso mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Remorse\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[envergonhar]{envergonhar — to embarrass, to shame}

\label{lesson:PT-C480-envergonhar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for regret, then the Portuguese for remorse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: envergonhar}
\textbf{envergonhar} — \textquotedblleft{}to embarrass, to shame\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
As notas más envergonharam o rapaz.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The bad marks made the boy ashamed.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Envergonhar-se} — to be ashamed.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{envergonhar} is built on \emph{vergonha} \textquotedblleft{}shame\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited from Latin \emph{verēcundia} \textquotedblleft{}modesty, shame\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[envergonhado]{envergonhado — ashamed, embarrassed; shy}

\label{lesson:PT-C480-envergonhado}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for remorse, then the Portuguese for to embarrass.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: envergonhado}
\textbf{envergonhado} — \textquotedblleft{}ashamed, embarrassed; shy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Fiquei envergonhado quando me enganei no nome dela.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I was embarrassed when I got her name wrong.}
\end{quote}

Also shy: \emph{uma criança envergonhada}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{envergonhado} goes back to Old Portuguese \emph{envergonnado} (EtymDB), the participle of \emph{envergonhar}, built on \emph{vergonha} \textquotedblleft{}shame\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{verēcundia}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
